why: Only the parity of each result matters, and both + and x commute with taking mod 2, so you can reduce every value mod 2 and evaluate the alternating chain on bits. It sits in the math week as modular arithmetic: (a*b) % 2 and (a+b) % 2 depend only on a % 2 and b % 2.
hints: The real results can be astronomically large, but you only need them mod 2.
Reduce each value with % 2 (Python gives 0 or 1 even for negatives) and apply the same alternating multiply, add, multiply, ... steps on bits.
Evaluate A[0::2] and A[1::2] separately in one pass each, then compare the two bits. O(n) time, O(1) extra.
pitfalls: Both groups start with multiplication: first * second + third * fourth ... evaluated strictly left to right, not with operator precedence.
In languages where -3 % 2 == -1, normalise to 0 or 1.
A group with a single element just returns that element mod 2.
